close_reason: Resolved together with PKIX-hy2e.1 as a single shared-shape fix. See PKIX-hy2e.1 close note for the full rationale (documentation + trait rustdoc + regression tests for the operator mutual-exclusion contract). All three sibling SMIME/TLS lints (Rfc6125TlsServerSanLint, Rfc8398SmimeSanLint, Rfc8551EkuEmailProtectionLint) received the same '# Use-case applicability — operator contract' rustdoc treatment.
description: Same systemic issue as PKIX-hy2e.1, filed separately because the fixes are in different modules. Trigger and bad behavior identical: each lint declares applies_to() = SubjectKind::Leaf and applies its rule to every leaf regardless of intended cert use case. - rfc6125::Rfc6125TlsServerSanLint requires SAN dNSName or iPAddress — wrong for S/MIME leaves and code-signing leaves. - rfc8398::Rfc8398SmimeSanLint requires SAN rfc822Name or SmtpUTF8Mailbox — wrong for TLS server leaves and code-signing leaves. - rfc8551::Rfc8551EkuEmailProtectionLint requires EKU id-kp-emailProtection — wrong for TLS server leaves and code-signing leaves. Concrete contradiction: there is NO single leaf certificate that satisfies all four lints (rfc5280 EKU server-auth + rfc6125 TLS-server SAN + rfc8398 S/MIME SAN + rfc8551 emailProtection EKU) at once. A caller who naively registers 'all the RFC-conformance lints' against any leaf gets at least 2 mutually-exclusive Error findings. The pkix-profiles crate's BasicTlsProfile and BasicSmimeProfile presumably register only the appropriate subset, but the lints themselves don't enforce this and the rustdoc doesn't document that each lint is use-case-specific. Tracked as a single fix because the four lints share the same shape problem and the resolution is one design decision.
title: Rfc6125TlsServerSanLint and Rfc8398SmimeSanLint share the Rfc5280EkuServerAuthLint false-positive shape
